title: Revamp scenario sequencer and introduce incremental-batch executor
creator: Maya Chen
description: Replace monolithic scenario driver with a pluggable scenario sequencer and add an incremental-batch executor to reduce tail latency and memory churn during large synthetic load runs. This work addresses long-standing issues: high variance in end-to-end load tests, adapter coupling between scenario orchestration and transport layers, and stale third-party dependencies in the runner. The goal is a smaller runtime surface for plugins, clearer lifecycle hooks for KV cache priming/eviction, and a drop-in compatibility shim for existing scenario definitions.
acceptance_criteria: Sequencer exposes a documented plugin API and a compatibility shim for legacy scenario JSON
Incremental-batch executor runs stable at 100k requests/min on staging without OOMs for 60m
End-to-end regression runs show <=5% change in median latency and no >10% increase in p95 for existing golden workloads
CI includes a lightweight smoke job for the new sequencer and executor and passes in the main pipeline
Migration plan and one-week canary rollout documented; feature flags available for toggling per-namespace
tasks: Define plugin surface and lifecycle hooks (init, pre-batch, post-batch, teardown)
Implement incremental-batch executor with backpressure-aware scheduling and soft memory cap
Add compatibility shim translating legacy scenario steps into sequencer plugins
Upgrade async runtime from tokio 1.10 -> 1.18 and bump related crates (reqwest, tonic) with test matrix
Instrument tracing and metrics for batch sizes, queueing delay, and memory pressure
Add CI smoke job and perf regression dashboard panel; add rollback plan
